1.explanation: The NUMBERS constant in src/languages/c-like.js defines the regex variants used to match numeric literals and their suffixes. Currently the decimal‐integer variant only allows single‐character suffixes (u|U|l|L|ul|UL|f|F|b|B), so a literal ending in “LL” only matches the first L and leaves the second L unmatched. To fix full LL (and other multi‐character suffixes) highlighting, the regex in NUMBERS must be expanded to recognize `ll`, `LL`, `llu`, `ULL`, etc. as valid suffix combinations.
1.bug_scenario: When highlighting C/C++ code with integer literals that use the LL suffix (e.g. 90LL, 467510400LL), only the first “L” is being consumed by the number regex and highlighted as part of the literal. The second “L” remains unhighlighted (or is treated as a separate token), so suffixes like “LL”, “llu”, “LLu” etc. are not fully recognized. See the “Dev test” screenshot showing “90LL” where only the first L is colored.

2.explanation: The NUMBERS constant in c-like.js defines the regular expressions used to identify and highlight numeric literals and their suffixes. The second variant’s suffix group only matches single-character suffixes (u|U|l|L|ul|UL|f|F|b|B) and does not include two-character suffixes like LL or ll. Because the regex stops matching after the first L, the second L falls outside the number token. To fix this bug, the suffix pattern in NUMBERS needs to be extended to explicitly recognize multi-character suffixes (e.g. LL, ll, ULL, etc.).
2.bug_scenario: In C/C++ code snippets where an integer literal is suffixed with “LL” (e.g. 467510400LL), only the first “L” is being picked up and highlighted as part of the numeric literal. The second “L” remains un–highlighted, leading to inconsistent styling for suffixes like LL, ll, ULL, etc.
